- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## npx
NotebookLM MCP - Access NotebookLM (notebooklm.google.com).

**Auth:** If you get authentication errors, run `nlm login` via your Bash/terminal tool. This is the automated authentication method that handles everything. Only use save_auth_tokens as a fallback if the CLI fails.
**Account Switching:** To switch Google Accounts for the MCP server, run `nlm login switch <profile>` in Bash. The MCP server instantly uses the active default profile.
**Confirmation:** Tools with confirm param require user approval before setting confirm=True.
**Studio:** After creating audio/video/infographic/slides, poll studio_status for completion.

- source_add(source_type=url|text|drive|file, url=..., document_id=..., text=..., file_path=...): Add any source type
- studio_create(artifact_type=audio|video|...): Create any artifact type

attachment.content:
- skills: Reference codebase for Crates. Use this skill when you need to understand the structure, implementation patterns, or code details of the Crates project.
- zeroclaw: Configure and operate ZeroClaw autonomous AI infrastructure. Use when user mentions zeroclaw CLI, needs to setup/configure zeroclaw, asks about 'zeroclaw providers', 'zeroclaw channels', 'autonomous AI agent', or wants to run LLMs on low-cost hardware (Raspberry Pi, ESP32, Arduino).
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# Schema-Coupled Plugin Blob Reflection Handoff
2	
3	Date: 2026-06-30
4	Repo: `operation-dbus-proto`
5	
6	## Current Direction
7	
8	The bridge has moved from a monolithic live schema mindset toward individual plugin object blobs.
9	
10	The settled model is:
11	
12	`PluginSchema` -> `PluginObjectBlob` -> active reflection catalog -> mounted tonic reflection service
13	
14	Key idea:
15	
16	- the schema is still the seed and source of truth
17	- the blob is the frozen runtime object for one plugin
18	- the caller sees only the relevant projection
19	- tonic reflection is static at build time, so the bridge now owns the mutable active catalog
20

# Schema-Coupled Plugin Blob Reflection Handoff

Date: 2026-06-30
Repo: `operation-dbus-proto`

## Current Direction

The bridge has moved from a monolithic live schema mindset toward individual plugin object blobs.

The settled model is:

`PluginSchema` -> `PluginObjectBlob` -> active reflection catalog -> mounted tonic reflection service

Key idea:

- the schema is still the seed and source of truth
- the blob is the frozen runtime object for one plugin
- the caller sees only the relevant projection
- tonic reflection is static at build time, so the bridge now owns the mutable active catalog

## What Was Added

### Generic blob support

File:

- [crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/plugin_object_blob.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/plugin_object_blob.rs)

Contains:

- `PluginObjectBlob`
- `DbusObjectIdentity`
- `GrpcObjectIdentity`
- `BlobMethod`
- `blobify_plugin_schema(...)`
- schema-derived `FileDescriptorSet` synthesis from `PluginSchema.methods`
- deterministic FNV-1a field number policy with protobuf reserved range skip
- canonical schema hashing helpers
- per-object shm naming helpers

### Zeroclaw consumer

File:

- [crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/zeroclaw_object_blob.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/zeroclaw_object_blob.rs)

Purpose:

- first plugin-specific consumer of the generic blob helper
- proves the shape for freezing D-Bus identity, gRPC identity, schema, and method metadata together

### Active reflection catalog

File:

- [crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/dynamic_reflection.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/dynamic_reflection.rs)

Purpose:

- maintain the active plugin blob set
- advertise only active service names
- answer reflection lookups from the active catalog

### Bridge wiring

File:

- [crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/grpc_server.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/grpc_server.rs)

Changes:

- `register_plugin_methods(...)` now freezes a `PluginObjectBlob`
- the blob is inserted into `active_reflection`
- v1 reflection is now built from `DynamicReflectionService`
- the bridge no longer relies on the old monolithic live schema for reflection identity

### Whitepaper

File:

- [docs/schema-coupled-plugin-blob-reflection-whitepaper.md](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/docs/schema-coupled-plugin-blob-reflection-whitepaper.md)

Contains:

- architecture summary
- blob model
- active reflection model
- D-Bus / gRPC / schema coupling
- risks and tests

## Verification

Passed:

- `cargo check -p op-grpc-bridge`
- `cargo test -p op-grpc-bridge dynamic_reflection --lib`
- `cargo test -p op-grpc-bridge zeroclaw_object_blob --lib`

Known warning:

- pre-existing `to_snake_case` dead code warning in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/proto_gen.rs`

## Important Constraints

- Do not reintroduce D-Bus passthrough as the public path for plugin methods.
- Do not treat the monolithic live schema as the runtime source of truth.
- Keep reflection aligned to mounted callable services only.
- Keep per-object blobs as the unit of active registration and removal.
- The blob can now synthesize richer typed descriptors from schema methods, but the generated tonic route service still uses `google.protobuf.Struct` request/response bodies until `build.rs` is upgraded to generate matching typed messages.

## Next Work

1. Move additional plugins onto `PluginObjectBlob` consumers one by one.
2. Upgrade `crates/op-grpc-bridge/build.rs` so generated tonic services use the same schema-derived request/response messages synthesized by the blob.
3. Replace any remaining live-schema-driven reflection paths with blob-driven registration.
4. Expand the active reflection catalog tests to cover non-Zeroclaw plugins.
5. Decide whether the per-object shm storage should stay JSON for now or move to a packed binary envelope.
6. Remove the old dead experimental reflection helpers once the blob path fully replaces them.

## Notes For Resume

1	# Schema-Coupled Plugin Object Blobs and Active gRPC Reflection
2	
3	Status: working design, first implementation pass in `op-grpc-bridge`
4	Date: 2026-06-30
5	
6	## Executive Summary
7	
8	The plugin system is moving from a monolithic live schema catalog toward individual, immutable plugin object blobs. Each blob is created when a D-Bus plugin object is created. The blob couples four identities that must not drift:
9	
10	- the `PluginSchema` identity
11	- the D-Bus object identity
12	- the generated gRPC service identity
13	- the gRPC reflection descriptor identity
14	
15	The schema remains the single source of truth. The blob is not a second source. It is the frozen projection of the schema into the bridge runtime, carrying enough metadata for D-Bus dispatch, gRPC method discovery, tonic reflection, GUI rendering, MCP/tool exposure, and compliance/audit indexing.
16	
17	The critical architectural correction is that `tonic_reflection::server::Builder` is static after build. It cannot add or remove services at runtime. Therefore active plugin discovery cannot be implemented by mutating tonic reflection directly. Instead, the bridge owns an active reflection catalog keyed by plugin object blobs. The reflection service reads this catalog when answering reflection requests.
18	
19	In practical terms:
20	
21	- D-Bus remains the authority and execution control plane.
22	- gRPC is the typed external and service-to-service transport.
23	- Clients discover callable gRPC methods through reflection.
24	- Reflection advertises active plugin object blobs, not the full universe of possible schemas.
25	- The old monolithic `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` shape becomes compatibility input only, not the target runtime model.
26	
27	## Non-Negotiable Rules
28	
29	1. `PluginSchema` is the source of truth.
30	2. A plugin object exists only if its schema can produce a valid object blob.
31	3. Every plugin object blob is created alongside its D-Bus object.
32	4. The blob must contain the D-Bus identity and the gRPC identity.
33	5. The blob must contain method metadata copied from `PluginSchema.methods`.
34	6. Reflection must advertise only callable mounted gRPC services.
35	7. No phantom reflection descriptors: if a method appears in reflection, the route must exist.
36	8. D-Bus passthrough is not the future public API.
37	9. Per-object blobs replace monolithic live schema as the runtime shape.
38	10. The Sled/shared memory path stores blobs as object artifacts, not a global polling database.
39	
40	## Terminology
41	
42	`PluginSchema`
43	: The canonical contract. Methods, side effects, capabilities, metadata, JSON rendering shape, and state schema derive from here.
44	
45	Plugin object blob
46	: The frozen bridge-local projection of one plugin schema and one D-Bus object identity into one gRPC/reflection identity.
47	
48	Active reflection catalog
49	: The bridge-owned runtime index of active blobs. It answers reflection list and descriptor lookups.
50	
51	D-Bus object
52	: The authoritative local object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`.
53	
54	Generated gRPC method service
55	: A tonic service generated from plugin schemas at build time, currently under `operation.plugin.v1.<Plugin>PluginMethods`.
56	
57	Descriptor set
58	: Encoded protobuf `FileDescriptorSet` bytes used by reflection clients to discover services, methods, and messages.
59	
60	## Target Data Model
61	
62	Each plugin object blob carries:
63	
64	```text
65	PluginObjectBlob
66	  plugin_id
67	  schema_version
68	  schema_hash
69	  schema_json
70	  dbus
71	    bus_name
72	    object_path
73	    interface_name
74	  grpc
75	    package
76	    service_name
77	    descriptor_set
78	  methods[]
79	    schema_name
80	    grpc_name
81	    grpc_path
82	    subid
83	    required_capability
84	    side_effect
85	    idempotent
86	    args_schema
87	    returns_schema
88	```
89	
90	This is deliberately redundant at the blob boundary. The schema is still authoritative, but the blob must be self-describing enough that reflection, GUI, compliance, and dispatch can reason about the same object without reassembling identity from scattered files.
91	
92	## Blob Creation Pipeline
93	
94	1. The plugin defines or returns `PluginSchema`.
95	2. The plugin is instantiated as a D-Bus object.
96	3. The bridge creates a `PluginObjectBlob`.
97	4. The bridge canonicalizes the schema JSON.
98	5. The bridge computes the schema hash.
99	6. The bridge derives D-Bus identity.
100	7. The bridge derives gRPC identity.
101	8. The bridge copies method metadata from `PluginSchema.methods`.
102	9. The bridge attaches descriptor bytes for the callable gRPC service surface.
103	10. The bridge inserts the blob into the active reflection catalog.
104	11. The reflection catalog rebuilds its service/symbol/file index.
105	12. gRPC reflection clients now see the active plugin service.
106	
107	Removal is the inverse:
108	
109	1. The D-Bus object is removed or deactivated.
110	2. The bridge removes the plugin object blob from the active catalog.
111	3. The reflection catalog rebuilds its advertised service list.
112	4. Reflection no longer lists that plugin service.
113	
114	The descriptor files can remain indexed while service advertisement changes. This lets `file_containing_symbol` and `file_by_filename` keep working for known generated descriptors while `list_services` reflects active objects.
115	
116	## Why Not Monolithic Live Schema
117	
118	The monolithic live schema file is useful as a bootstrap and compatibility artifact, but it is the wrong runtime primitive.
119	
120	Problems with monolithic live schema:
121	
122	- It blurs object identity and schema inventory.
123	- It makes active/inactive plugin state ambiguous.
124	- It encourages polling.
125	- It turns runtime discovery into catalog scraping instead of object registration.
126	- It does not naturally couple D-Bus object path, gRPC service name, reflection bytes, and method dispatch metadata.
127	- It makes partial updates risky because one file represents too many unrelated objects.
128	
129	Per-object blobs solve this:
130	
131	- one D-Bus object, one blob
132	- one schema hash, one blob identity
133	- one gRPC service identity, one blob
134	- one artifact to hash, audit, publish, remove, or replay
135	
136	The eventual shared memory layout should look like object blobs, not a single mutable schema registry:
137	
138	```text
139	/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/
140	  zeroclaw.<schema_hash>.blob.json
141	  wireguard.<schema_hash>.blob.json
142	  persona.<schema_hash>.blob.json
143	```
144	
145	The exact storage can later become binary, mmap-backed, or sled-backed. The important point is object granularity.
146	
147	## Reflection Model
148	
149	Tonic reflection has two separate concerns:
150	
151	1. Descriptor availability
152	2. Service advertisement
153	
154	Descriptor availability means the server can return `FileDescriptorProto` bytes for files, messages, services, and methods.
155	
156	Service advertisement means `ListServices` returns the services clients should consider active and callable.
157	
158	The current implementation direction separates these:
159	
160	- descriptor files come from compiled descriptor sets
161	- active service names come from active plugin object blobs
162	
163	This prevents reflection from listing unmounted or inactive services while still allowing the bridge to use generated descriptor files.
164	
165	The blob helper now also synthesizes a plugin-level `FileDescriptorSet` directly from `PluginSchema.methods`. This closes the self-contained blob identity gap: the blob no longer needs an externally supplied descriptor set. The remaining implementation step is to make the mounted tonic service generation use the same request/response message synthesis, because reflection must never advertise a typed body that the mounted route does not accept.
166	
167	## Why tonic-reflection Builder Is Not Enough
168	
169	`tonic_reflection::server::Builder` accepts descriptor sets, indexes them, and returns a reflection service. Once built, that service has no supported mutation API.
170	
171	This means it cannot:
172	
173	- add a plugin service after server startup
174	- remove a plugin service after D-Bus object removal
175	- re-index per-object blobs as they become active
176	- represent active object lifetime
177	
178	The bridge-owned `ActiveReflectionCatalog` fixes this by becoming the mutable layer. The reflection server reads from that catalog instead of from tonic's private immutable index.
179	
180	## ActiveReflectionCatalog Responsibilities
181	
182	The active reflection catalog owns:
183	
184	- active plugin blobs
185	- descriptor sets
186	- filename index
187	- symbol index
188	- active service list
189	
190	It must support:
191	
192	- `upsert_blob(blob)`
193	- `remove_blob(plugin_id)`
194	- `list_services()`
195	- `file_by_filename(filename)`
196	- `symbol_by_name(symbol)`
197	
198	It rebuilds indexes after blob add/remove. This is acceptable because plugin object lifecycle is low-frequency compared with request handling. If needed later, the index can become incremental.
199	
200	## Generated gRPC Method Shape
201	
202	The currently mounted first-pass generated method services use:
203	
204	```proto
205	package operation.plugin.v1;
206	
207	import "google/protobuf/struct.proto";
208	
209	service ZeroclawPluginMethods {
210	  rpc GetState(google.protobuf.Struct) returns (google.protobuf.Struct);
211	}
212	```
213	
214	This is intentionally pragmatic. It gives each plugin a real tonic service and each method a real reflected RPC path while avoiding an immediate explosion of generated request/response message types.
215	
216	The second pass can make methods fully typed:
217	
218	```proto
219	service ZeroclawPluginMethods {
220	  rpc RegisterAgent(RegisterAgentRequest) returns (RegisterAgentResponse);
221	}
222	```
223	
224	That second pass should still be generated from `PluginSchema.methods`, not hand-authored proto files.
225	
226	The blob descriptor synthesis has already moved toward the second-pass shape by deriving request and response messages from `MethodDecl.args` and `MethodDecl.returns`. `build.rs` still needs to generate matching tonic services before those richer descriptors become the externally advertised callable reflection contract.
227	
228	## D-Bus Dispatch Model
229	
230	The generated gRPC method handlers do not become the authority. They are transport handlers.
231	
232	The handler flow is:
233	
234	1. gRPC request arrives.
235	2. Ghostbridge identity/capability metadata is read.
236	3. Required method capability is checked against schema metadata.
237	4. Request payload is converted into schema-shaped JSON.
238	5. The bridge dispatches the method through the mutation engine.
239	6. The mutation engine calls the D-Bus object method.
240	7. The D-Bus result is converted back into gRPC response shape.
241	
242	This keeps D-Bus as the execution authority while removing the need for external clients to call D-Bus passthrough.
243	
244	## D-Bus Passthrough Position
245	
246	D-Bus passthrough is a compatibility and debugging surface, not the target API.
247	
248	The goal is not to remove D-Bus. The goal is to stop exposing raw D-Bus passthrough where a schema-generated gRPC method exists.
249	
250	Target rule:
251	
252	- If a plugin method exists in `PluginSchema.methods`, clients call the generated gRPC method.
253	- The bridge internally dispatches through D-Bus.
254	- Passthrough remains only for transition, emergency inspection, or objects not yet converted.
255	
256	## Introspection Position
257	
258	D-Bus introspection is useful for generation and audit, not as the runtime contract.
259	
260	Good uses:
261	
262	- detect methods that exist on D-Bus but are missing from schema
263	- detect schema methods that are not implemented on D-Bus
264	- bootstrap an auto plugin generator
265	- create migration reports
266	- verify object consistency during tests
267	
268	Bad uses:
269	
270	- replacing `PluginSchema` as the source of truth
271	- generating ad hoc runtime method contracts
272	- allowing untyped passthrough to become the main API again
273	
274	The auto plugin generator should use introspection as evidence, then write/update schema-owned method declarations.
275	
276	## Schemars Position
277	
278	Schemars is the seed for state and input/output schema generation. It is not enough by itself to define the full plugin contract because methods, side effects, capability requirements, subids, and gRPC identity need operational metadata.
279	
280	The right layering is:
281	
282	```text
283	Rust state/input/output structs
284	  -> schemars JSON Schema
285	  -> PluginSchema methods/properties/metadata
286	  -> PluginObjectBlob
287	  -> D-Bus object + gRPC service + reflection
288	```
289	
290	The old confusion came from helper files looking like schema definition files. The cleaner pattern is:
291	
292	- plugin owns the schema contract
293	- schemars derives structural JSON schema
294	- helper/scaffold code processes output
295	- blob freezes the projection
296	
297	## Compliance Metadata
298	
299	Every method blob should carry at minimum:
300	
301	- `subid`
302	- `required_capability`
303	- `side_effect`
304	- `idempotent`
305	- schema hash
306	- object path
307	- gRPC path
308	
309	Future compliance metadata should include:
310	
311	- `uuid`
312	- `control_refs`
313	- `statement_refs`
314	- `control_source`
315	- `actor_id` requirements for mutations
316	- `capability_id` requirements
317	- event hash linkage
318	- Snowball session ledger references
319	
320	The blob is the right place to attach this because it is where schema, D-Bus identity, gRPC method identity, and reflection identity meet.
321	
322	## First Implementation Pass
323	
324	The first pass should prove the full path with representative plugins:
325	
326	- Zeroclaw
327	- Wireguard
328	- Keypair
329	- Identity
330	- Persona
331	- Qdrant
332	- Netmaker
333	- Cozo
334	
335	Minimum success criteria:
336	
337	- each plugin has a valid `PluginSchema`
338	- each plugin has methods in `PluginSchema.methods`
339	- each plugin can produce a `PluginObjectBlob`
340	- each blob has a schema hash
341	- each blob has D-Bus identity
342	- each blob has gRPC identity
343	- each blob has method metadata
344	- active reflection advertises each active blob service
345	- generated gRPC method routes dispatch through D-Bus/mutation engine
346	- reflection does not advertise inactive blobs
347	
348	## Second Implementation Pass
349	
350	The second pass should increase type fidelity:
351	
352	- generate per-method request messages from `method.args`
353	- generate per-method response messages from `method.returns`
354	- remove generic `google.protobuf.Struct` where schemas are stable enough
355	- enrich blob metadata with compliance controls
356	- write blobs to the object-level shared memory layout
357	- add D-Bus introspection audit checks
358	- add test fixtures for all high-value plugins
359	
360	## Risks
361	
362	Descriptor drift
363	: Reflection advertises a method whose route is not mounted. This is the worst client-facing failure and must be guarded by tests.
364	
365	Schema drift
366	: D-Bus implementation has methods not represented in `PluginSchema.methods`.
367	
368	Blob drift
369	: Blob metadata no longer matches the schema hash or D-Bus object path.
370	
371	Monolithic fallback creep
372	: Old `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` remains treated as runtime truth instead of compatibility input.
373	
374	Passthrough creep
375	: Clients keep using D-Bus passthrough even after generated gRPC methods exist.
376	
377	Over-generation
378	: Generated proto services expose methods for plugins that are not active. Active reflection must filter service advertisement.
379	
380	## Required Tests
381	
382	Blob tests:
383	
384	- blob contains canonical schema bytes
385	- blob hash is stable for the same schema
386	- blob D-Bus path matches plugin id
387	- blob gRPC service name matches generated service
388	- blob methods match `PluginSchema.methods`
389	
390	Reflection tests:
391

# Schema-Coupled Plugin Object Blobs and Active gRPC Reflection

Status: working design, first implementation pass in `op-grpc-bridge`
Date: 2026-06-30

## Executive Summary

The plugin system is moving from a monolithic live schema catalog toward individual, immutable plugin object blobs. Each blob is created when a D-Bus plugin object is created. The blob couples four identities that must not drift:

- the `PluginSchema` identity
- the D-Bus object identity
- the generated gRPC service identity
- the gRPC reflection descriptor identity

The schema remains the single source of truth. The blob is not a second source. It is the frozen projection of the schema into the bridge runtime, carrying enough metadata for D-Bus dispatch, gRPC method discovery, tonic reflection, GUI rendering, MCP/tool exposure, and compliance/audit indexing.

The critical architectural correction is that `tonic_reflection::server::Builder` is static after build. It cannot add or remove services at runtime. Therefore active plugin discovery cannot be implemented by mutating tonic reflection directly. Instead, the bridge owns an active reflection catalog keyed by plugin object blobs. The reflection service reads this catalog when answering reflection requests.

In practical terms:

- D-Bus remains the authority and execution control plane.
- gRPC is the typed external and service-to-service transport.
- Clients discover callable gRPC methods through reflection.
- Reflection advertises active plugin object blobs, not the full universe of possible schemas.
- The old monolithic `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` shape becomes compatibility input only, not the target runtime model.

## Non-Negotiable Rules

1. `PluginSchema` is the source of truth.
2. A plugin object exists only if its schema can produce a valid object blob.
3. Every plugin object blob is created alongside its D-Bus object.
4. The blob must contain the D-Bus identity and the gRPC identity.
5. The blob must contain method metadata copied from `PluginSchema.methods`.
6. Reflection must advertise only callable mounted gRPC services.
7. No phantom reflection descriptors: if a method appears in reflection, the route must exist.
8. D-Bus passthrough is not the future public API.
9. Per-object blobs replace monolithic live schema as the runtime shape.
10. The Sled/shared memory path stores blobs as object artifacts, not a global polling database.

## Terminology

`PluginSchema`
: The canonical contract. Methods, side effects, capabilities, metadata, JSON rendering shape, and state schema derive from here.

Plugin object blob
: The frozen bridge-local projection of one plugin schema and one D-Bus object identity into one gRPC/reflection identity.

Active reflection catalog
: The bridge-owned runtime index of active blobs. It answers reflection list and descriptor lookups.

D-Bus object
: The authoritative local object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`.

Generated gRPC method service
: A tonic service generated from plugin schemas at build time, currently under `operation.plugin.v1.<Plugin>PluginMethods`.

Descriptor set
: Encoded protobuf `FileDescriptorSet` bytes used by reflection clients to discover services, methods, and messages.

## Target Data Model

Each plugin object blob carries:

```text
PluginObjectBlob
  plugin_id
  schema_version
  schema_hash
  schema_json
  dbus
    bus_name
    object_path
    interface_name
  grpc
    package
    service_name
    descriptor_set
  methods[]
    schema_name
    grpc_name
    grpc_path
    subid
    required_capability
    side_effect
    idempotent
    args_schema
    returns_schema
```

This is deliberately redundant at the blob boundary. The schema is still authoritative, but the blob must be self-describing enough that reflection, GUI, compliance, and dispatch can reason about the same object without reassembling identity from scattered files.

## Blob Creation Pipeline

1. The plugin defines or returns `PluginSchema`.
2. The plugin is instantiated as a D-Bus object.
3. The bridge creates a `PluginObjectBlob`.
4. The bridge canonicalizes the schema JSON.
5. The bridge computes the schema hash.
6. The bridge derives D-Bus identity.
7. The bridge derives gRPC identity.
8. The bridge copies method metadata from `PluginSchema.methods`.
9. The bridge attaches descriptor bytes for the callable gRPC service surface.
10. The bridge inserts the blob into the active reflection catalog.
11. The reflection catalog rebuilds its service/symbol/file index.
12. gRPC reflection clients now see the active plugin service.

Removal is the inverse:

1. The D-Bus object is removed or deactivated.
2. The bridge removes the plugin object blob from the active catalog.
3. The reflection catalog rebuilds its advertised service list.
4. Reflection no longer lists that plugin service.

The descriptor files can remain indexed while service advertisement changes. This lets `file_containing_symbol` and `file_by_filename` keep working for known generated descriptors while `list_services` reflects active objects.

## Why Not Monolithic Live Schema

The monolithic live schema file is useful as a bootstrap and compatibility artifact, but it is the wrong runtime primitive.

Problems with monolithic live schema:

- It blurs object identity and schema inventory.
- It makes active/inactive plugin state ambiguous.
- It encourages polling.
- It turns runtime discovery into catalog scraping instead of object registration.
- It does not naturally couple D-Bus object path, gRPC service name, reflection bytes, and method dispatch metadata.
- It makes partial updates risky because one file represents too many unrelated objects.

Per-object blobs solve this:

- one D-Bus object, one blob
- one schema hash, one blob identity
- one gRPC service identity, one blob
- one artifact to hash, audit, publish, remove, or replay

The eventual shared memory layout should look like object blobs, not a single mutable schema registry:

```text
/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/
  zeroclaw.<schema_hash>.blob.json
  wireguard.<schema_hash>.blob.json
  persona.<schema_hash>.blob.json
```

The exact storage can later become binary, mmap-backed, or sled-backed. The important point is object granularity.

## Reflection Model

Tonic reflection has two separate concerns:

1. Descriptor availability
2. Service advertisement

Descriptor availability means the server can return `FileDescriptorProto` bytes for files, messages, services, and methods.

Service advertisement means `ListServices` returns the services clients should consider active and callable.

The current implementation direction separates these:

- descriptor files come from compiled descriptor sets
- active service names come from active plugin object blobs

This prevents reflection from listing unmounted or inactive services while still allowing the bridge to use generated descriptor files.

The blob helper now also synthesizes a plugin-level `FileDescriptorSet` directly from `PluginSchema.methods`. This closes the self-contained blob identity gap: the blob no longer needs an externally supplied descriptor set. The remaining implementation step is to make the mounted tonic service generation use the same request/response message synthesis, because reflection must never advertise a typed body that the mounted route does not accept.

## Why tonic-reflection Builder Is Not Enough

`tonic_reflection::server::Builder` accepts descriptor sets, indexes them, and returns a reflection service. Once built, that service has no supported mutation API.

This means it cannot:

- add a plugin service after server startup
- remove a plugin service after D-Bus object removal
- re-index per-object blobs as they become active
- represent active object lifetime

The bridge-owned `ActiveReflectionCatalog` fixes this by becoming the mutable layer. The reflection server reads from that catalog instead of from tonic's private immutable index.

## ActiveReflectionCatalog Responsibilities

The active reflection catalog owns:

- active plugin blobs
- descriptor sets
- filename index
- symbol index
- active service list

It must support:

- `upsert_blob(blob)`
- `remove_blob(plugin_id)`
- `list_services()`
- `file_by_filename(filename)`
- `symbol_by_name(symbol)`

It rebuilds indexes after blob add/remove. This is acceptable because plugin object lifecycle is low-frequency compared with request handling. If needed later, the index can become incremental.

## Generated gRPC Method Shape

The currently mounted first-pass generated method services use:

```proto
package operation.plugin.v1;

import "google/protobuf/struct.proto";

service ZeroclawPluginMethods {
  rpc GetState(google.protobuf.Struct) returns (google.protobuf.Struct);
}
```

This is intentionally pragmatic. It gives each plugin a real tonic service and each method a real reflected RPC path while avoiding an immediate explosion of generated request/response message types.

The second pass can make methods fully typed:

```proto
service ZeroclawPluginMethods {
  rpc RegisterAgent(RegisterAgentRequest) returns (RegisterAgentResponse);
}
```

That second pass should still be generated from `PluginSchema.methods`, not hand-authored proto files.

The blob descriptor synthesis has already moved toward the second-pass shape by deriving request and response messages from `MethodDecl.args` and `MethodDecl.returns`. `build.rs` still needs to generate matching tonic services before those richer descriptors become the externally advertised callable reflection contract.

## D-Bus Dispatch Model

The generated gRPC method handlers do not become the authority. They are transport handlers.

The handler flow is:

1. gRPC request arrives.
2. Ghostbridge identity/capability metadata is read.
3. Required method capability is checked against schema metadata.
4. Request payload is converted into schema-shaped JSON.
5. The bridge dispatches the method through the mutation engine.
6. The mutation engine calls the D-Bus object method.
7. The D-Bus result is converted back into gRPC response shape.

This keeps D-Bus as the execution authority while removing the need for external clients to call D-Bus passthrough.

## D-Bus Passthrough Position

D-Bus passthrough is a compatibility and debugging surface, not the target API.

The goal is not to remove D-Bus. The goal is to stop exposing raw D-Bus passthrough where a schema-generated gRPC method exists.

Target rule:

- If a plugin method exists in `PluginSchema.methods`, clients call the generated gRPC method.
- The bridge internally dispatches through D-Bus.
- Passthrough remains only for transition, emergency inspection, or objects not yet converted.

## Introspection Position

D-Bus introspection is useful for generation and audit, not as the runtime contract.

Good uses:

- detect methods that exist on D-Bus but are missing from schema
- detect schema methods that are not implemented on D-Bus
- bootstrap an auto plugin generator
- create migration reports
- verify object consistency during tests

Bad uses:

- replacing `PluginSchema` as the source of truth
- generating ad hoc runtime method contracts
- allowing untyped passthrough to become the main API again

The auto plugin generator should use introspection as evidence, then write/update schema-owned method declarations.

## Schemars Position

Schemars is the seed for state and input/output schema generation. It is not enough by itself to define the full plugin contract because methods, side effects, capability requirements, subids, and gRPC identity need operational metadata.

The right layering is:

```text
Rust state/input/output structs
  -> schemars JSON Schema
  -> PluginSchema methods/properties/metadata
  -> PluginObjectBlob
  -> D-Bus object + gRPC service + reflection
```

The old confusion came from helper files looking like schema definition files. The cleaner pattern is:

- plugin owns the schema contract
- schemars derives structural JSON schema
- helper/scaffold code processes output
- blob freezes the projection

## Compliance Metadata

Every method blob should carry at minimum:

- `subid`
- `required_capability`
- `side_effect`
- `idempotent`
- schema hash
- object path
- gRPC path

Future compliance metadata should include:

- `uuid`
- `control_refs`
- `statement_refs`
- `control_source`
- `actor_id` requirements for mutations
- `capability_id` requirements
- event hash linkage
- Snowball session ledger references

The blob is the right place to attach this because it is where schema, D-Bus identity, gRPC method identity, and reflection identity meet.

## First Implementation Pass

The first pass should prove the full path with representative plugins:

- Zeroclaw
- Wireguard
- Keypair
- Identity
- Persona
- Qdrant
- Netmaker
- Cozo

Minimum success criteria:

- each plugin has a valid `PluginSchema`
- each plugin has methods in `PluginSchema.methods`
- each plugin can produce a `PluginObjectBlob`
- each blob has a schema hash
- each blob has D-Bus identity
- each blob has gRPC identity
- each blob has method metadata
- active reflection advertises each active blob service
- generated gRPC method routes dispatch through D-Bus/mutation engine
- reflection does not advertise inactive blobs

## Second Implementation Pass

The second pass should increase type fidelity:

- generate per-method request messages from `method.args`
- generate per-method response messages from `method.returns`
- remove generic `google.protobuf.Struct` where schemas are stable enough
- enrich blob metadata with compliance controls
- write blobs to the object-level shared memory layout
- add D-Bus introspection audit checks
- add test fixtures for all high-value plugins

## Risks

Descriptor drift
: Reflection advertises a method whose route is not mounted. This is the worst client-facing failure and must be guarded by tests.

Schema drift
: D-Bus implementation has methods not represented in `PluginSchema.methods`.

Blob drift
: Blob metadata no longer matches the schema hash or D-Bus object path.

Monolithic fallback creep
: Old `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` remains treated as runtime truth instead of compatibility input.

Passthrough creep
: Clients keep using D-Bus passthrough even after generated gRPC methods exist.

Over-generation
: Generated proto services expose methods for plugins that are not active. Active reflection must filter service advertisement.

## Required Tests

Blob tests:

- blob contains canonical schema bytes
- blob hash is stable for the same schema
- blob D-Bus path matches plugin id
- blob gRPC service name matches generated service
- blob methods match `PluginSchema.methods`

Reflection tests:

- inactive plugin service is not listed
- inserting blob lists service
- removing blob removes service
- `file_by_filename` returns descriptor bytes
- `file_containing_symbol` returns descriptor bytes for active service

Dispatch tests:

- generated gRPC method reaches mutation engine
- capability denial happens before dispatch
- method args are converted correctly
- method result is converted correctly

Introspection audit tests:

- D-Bus method missing from schema is reported
- schema method missing from D-Bus is reported
- method signature mismatch is reported

## Current Code Landmarks

`crates/op-grpc-bridge/build.rs`
: Generates `operation.plugin.v1.<Plugin>PluginMethods` services from loaded plugin schemas.

`crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/plugin_object_blob.rs`
: Generic plugin object blob model and blobification helper.

`crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/zeroclaw_object_blob.rs`
: First plugin-specific blob consumer.

`crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/dynamic_reflection.rs`
: Active reflection catalog and v1 reflection service.

`crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/grpc_server.rs`
: Registers plugin method blobs and mounts the reflection service.

`crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/callable_reflection.rs`
: Static callable descriptor snapshot from compiled tonic descriptor bytes.

## Final Architecture Statement

The plugin schema is the seed. The D-Bus object is the authority. The plugin object blob is the frozen runtime identity. The generated gRPC service is the callable transport. Active reflection is the discovery surface. The Sled/shared memory layer stores object blobs, not a monolithic schema database.

That gives the system a clean chain:

```text
PluginSchema
  -> PluginObjectBlob
  -> D-Bus object authority
  -> generated gRPC methods
  -> active reflection discovery
  -> GUI/MCP/client typed calls
  -> Snowball/compliance audit trail
```

# Plugin Schema Refactor Guidance

This document preserves the core instructions for continuing the plugin-as-schema refactor in the
control-plane chatbot context. Keep it in sync with the live refactor so the next run can pick up
without re-explaining the architecture.

## Core Rules
- The plugin owns a single canonical JSON-RCP document (`ctl-plane-chatbot` example) that carries
  schema, footprint policy, privacy instructions, tags, and metadata. Everything downstream reads
  through that document.
- `op_plugins::PluginCatalog`/`PluginRegistry` is the runtime catalog/cache. It **does not create new
  schema**; it hydrates from the persisted `op_dbus_model::SqlitePluginCatalog` (a.k.a. the schema
  catalog store) and exposes `SchemaCatalog`/`SchemaRegistry` as a read-only index.
- `SchemaCatalog` is the shared lookup/composition layer for validation, JSON rendering, vectorization,
  and compatibility exports. Rename callers to the catalog terminology, but keep compatibility aliases
  for the short term.
- Registration order: plugin code builds schema → canonical document → persist to catalog store → update
  in-memory catalog → export D-Bus/grpc projections.

## Operational Notes
- When rate-limited (Voyage or Cargo), pause embedding/indexing work and fall back to cached catalog
  copies; resume once the throttle lifts.
- If you are blocked mid-refactor, capture the last command outputs (cargo check/test) so the next
  iteration knows what failed.
- Keep the QA list minimal: `cargo check -p op-plugins`, `op-state(-store)`, `op-grpc-bridge`, `op-dbus-model`.

## To Do Next Time
1. Finish rehydrating startup so the catalog seeds from persisted documents before calling
   `PluginRegistry::register` (makes persisted authority the ground floor).
2. Remove any code still inferring schema by sampling live state (`build_plugin_schema` fallback) once
   all plugins ship explicit `schema()` implementations.
3. Align the `ctl-plane-chatbot` Kiro spec with this architecture (metadata, reasoning episodes, vectors).

Notes on using grpc with rust and tonic
In the Tonic examples proto files are used to generated service and client stubs with tonic_build.

The Getting started section mentions the following:

For IntelliJ IDEA users, please refer to this and enable org.rust.cargo.evaluate.build.scripts experimental feature.

But in order to have a nice development experience you need some additional tweaks.

You can find the full code here: https://github.com/timvw/arrow-flightsql-odbc

By default the stubs are generated in ./target/…/build/… Unfortunately CLion does not scan those folders and you don’t get to benefit from intellisense.

As a workaround you can generate the stubs in your ./src folder instead. You can do that by configuring the tonic_build in build.rs.

While you are at it, you should also enable the writing of a file_descriptor_set to enable GRPC Server Reflection using tonic-reflection.

build.rs
use std::env;
use std::path::PathBuf;

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {

    //intellij does not easily find types when not adding code to src
    //tonic_build::compile_protos("proto/Flight.proto")?;
    //tonic_build::compile_protos("proto/FlightSql.proto")?;

    let original_out_dir = PathBuf::from(env::var("OUT_DIR")?);

    let out_dir = "./src";

    tonic_build::configure()
        .out_dir(out_dir)
        .file_descriptor_set_path(original_out_dir.join("flight_descriptor.bin"))
        .compile(&["proto/Flight.proto"], &["proto"])?;

    tonic_build::configure()
        .out_dir(out_dir)
        .file_descriptor_set_path(original_out_dir.join("flight_sql_descriptor.bin"))
        .compile(&["proto/FlightSql.proto"], &["proto"])?;

    Ok(())
}
Now you can update your lib.rs and include the generated stubs by referring to their path in ./src instead of the include_proto! macro. Notice that I have also used the include_file_descriptor_set to enable the GRPC Server Reflection:

src/lib.rs
/*
pub mod arrow_flight_protocol {
    tonic::include_proto!("arrow.flight.protocol"); // The string specified here must match the proto package name
}

pub mod arrow_flight_protocol_sql {
    tonic::include_proto!("arrow.flight.protocol.sql"); // The string specified here must match the proto package name
}
 */

#[path = "arrow.flight.protocol.rs"]
pub mod arrow_flight_protocol;

#[path = "arrow.flight.protocol.sql.rs"]
pub mod arrow_flight_protocol_sql;

pub const FLIGHT_DESCRIPTOR_SET: &[u8] = tonic::include_file_descriptor_set!("flight_descriptor");
pub const FLIGHT_SQL_DESCRIPTOR_SET: &[u8] = tonic::include_file_descriptor_set!("flight_sql_descriptor");
Now you can create your server and register the reflection service:

src/bin/server.rs
let reflection_server = tonic_reflection::server::Builder::configure()
    .register_encoded_file_descriptor_set(arrow_flightsql_odbc::FLIGHT_DESCRIPTOR_SET)
    .register_encoded_file_descriptor_set(arrow_flightsql_odbc::FLIGHT_SQL_DESCRIPTOR_SET)
    .build()?;

Server::builder()
    .add_service(FlightServiceServer::new(myserver))
    .add_service(reflection_server)
    .serve(addr)
    .await?;
When your server is running, you can query it:

grpcurl -vv -plaintext 'localhost:52358' list
Outputs:

arrow.flight.protocol.FlightService
grpc.reflection.v1alpha.ServerReflection
When diving a little deeper, we find the following:

grpcurl -vv -plaintext 'localhost:52358' list arrow.flight.protocol.FlightService
Outputs:

arrow.flight.protocol.FlightService.DoAction
arrow.flight.protocol.FlightService.DoExchange
arrow.flight.protocol.FlightService.DoGet
arrow.flight.protocol.FlightService.DoPut
arrow.flight.protocol.FlightService.GetFlightInfo
arrow.flight.protocol.FlightService.GetSchema
arrow.flight.protocol.FlightService.Handshake
arrow.flight.protocol.FlightService.ListActions
arrow.flight.protocol.FlightService.ListFlights
Happy coding!

This document details the architectural approach and technical implementation for dynamically synthesizing and serving `tonic` gRPC reflection for D-Bus services projected from `schemars`-generated JSON Schemas. In this system, each plugin's schema serves as the absolute source of truth—defining its object path, methods, properties, and signals—and is registered at runtime via `ZeroclawService::WatchSchema`.

The core challenge is that the `tonic-reflection` crate's `Builder` is designed for static, compile-time `FileDescriptorSet` registration and does not support runtime mutation after `.build()` is called. To overcome this, the recommended approach is to implement a custom, mutable `ServerReflection` service that wraps a dynamically updatable `prost_reflect::DescriptorPool`. This allows the system to programmatically construct `prost_types::FileDescriptorProto` definitions from incoming JSON Schemas and expose them instantly to gRPC clients via reflection, without requiring a server restart.

## 2. Architectural Approach

The solution requires bridging three distinct domains at runtime:
1. **Schema Parsing:** Deserializing the `schemars` JSON Schema to extract type definitions (`$defs`) and custom extensions (e.g., `x-methods`, `x-signals`).
2. **Descriptor Synthesis:** Translating the JSON Schema types into Protocol Buffer types and constructing `prost_types::FileDescriptorProto` instances programmatically.
3. **Dynamic Reflection Serving:** Managing these descriptors in a thread-safe `prost_reflect::DescriptorPool` and serving them via a custom implementation of the gRPC Server Reflection Protocol (`grpc.reflection.v1.ServerReflection`).

### 2.1 The Immutability of `tonic-reflection`

The standard `tonic_reflection::server::Builder` consumes registered `FileDescriptorSet`s and produces an immutable `ServerReflectionServer`. Internally, it indexes all files, services, messages, and enums into static `HashMap`s. There are no exposed APIs to mutate this state post-build. 

Therefore, relying on the built-in `tonic-reflection` service is insufficient for dynamic plugin registration. Instead, the system must implement the reflection protocol manually, backed by a mutable store.

## 3. Implementation Details

### 3.1 Schema to Protobuf Type Mapping

The declarative nature of JSON Schema must be mapped to the rigid, strongly-typed structure of Protocol Buffers. The following mapping strategy is recommended:

| JSON Schema Type / Keyword | Protobuf Field Type / Construct | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `string` | `TYPE_STRING` | Maps directly. |
| `integer` | `TYPE_INT64` | Default to 64-bit for maximum range. Use `format` hints for `TYPE_INT32`. |
| `number` | `TYPE_DOUBLE` | Default to double precision. Use `format` hints for `TYPE_FLOAT`. |
| `boolean` | `TYPE_BOOL` | Maps directly. |
| `array` | `LABEL_REPEATED` | The `items` keyword dictates the inner element type. |
| `object` | `TYPE_MESSAGE` | Translates to a nested `DescriptorProto`. |
| `null` / `nullable` | `optional` keyword | Mapped using proto3 `optional` presence. |
| `$ref` | `type_name` | Resolves to the fully qualified name of the referenced `DescriptorProto`. |
| `anyOf` / `oneOf` | `oneof` wrapper | Maps to a protobuf `oneof` group containing each variant. |

**Stable Field Numbering:** Protobuf requires stable field numbers. Because JSON Schema properties are unordered, field numbers must be assigned deterministically. A common approach is to compute a stable hash (e.g., FNV-1a or CRC32) of the field name, modulo the maximum valid protobuf field number (536,870,911), ensuring the result avoids the reserved range (19000-29999).

### 3.2 Programmatic Descriptor Synthesis

Using `prost-types`, the system constructs the descriptor tree from the bottom up:

1. **Messages:** Iterate over `$defs`. For each schema definition, create a `DescriptorProto`. Map its properties to `FieldDescriptorProto` entries using the mapping rules above.
2. **Services:** Extract `x-methods` from the schema. For each method, create a `MethodDescriptorProto`, specifying the fully qualified `input_type` and `output_type`.
3. **Files:** Wrap the messages and services in a `FileDescriptorProto`, assigning a unique package name (e.g., `plugin.v1.<plugin_id>`).

```rust

fn synthesize_plugin_descriptor(plugin_id: &str, schema: &schemars::schema::RootSchema) -> FileDescriptorProto {
    let mut file = FileDescriptorProto {
        name: Some(format!("{}.proto", plugin_id)),
        package: Some(format!("plugin.v1.{}", plugin_id)),
        syntax: Some("proto3".to_string()),
        ..Default::default()
    };

    // ... logic to convert schema.$defs to file.message_type ...
    
    // 2. Synthesize Service from x-methods
    // ... logic to convert custom methods extension to file.service ...
    
    file
}
```

### 3.3 Dynamic Descriptor Pool Management

The `prost-reflect` crate provides `DescriptorPool`, which manages dependencies and enables runtime introspection. The custom reflection service must maintain an `Arc<RwLock<DescriptorPool>>` to allow concurrent reads from reflection clients and exclusive writes during plugin registration.

When a new plugin registers:
1. Synthesize its `FileDescriptorProto`.
2. Acquire a write lock on the `DescriptorPool`.
3. Call `pool.add_file_descriptor_proto(file_proto)`.
4. Release the lock.

### 3.4 Custom Server Reflection Implementation

To serve the dynamically updated pool, implement the `grpc.reflection.v1.ServerReflection` trait. The `ServerReflectionInfo` RPC is a bidirectional stream. To overcome this, the recommended approach is to implement a custom, mutable `ServerReflection` service that wraps a dynamically updatable `prost_reflect::DescriptorPool`. This allows the system to programmatically construct `prost_types::FileDescriptorProto` definitions from incoming JSON Schemas and expose them instantly to gRPC clients via reflection, without requiring a server restart.
414	
415	## 2. Architectural Approach
416	
417	The solution requires bridging three distinct domains at runtime:
418	1. **Schema Parsing:** Deserializing the `schemars` JSON Schema to extract type definitions (`$defs`) and custom extensions (e.g., `x-methods`, `x-signals`).
419	2. **Descriptor Synthesis:** Translating the JSON Schema types into Protocol Buffer types and constructing `prost_types::FileDescriptorProto` instances programmatically.
420	3. **Dynamic Reflection Serving:** Managing these descriptors in a thread-safe `prost_reflect::DescriptorPool` and serving them via a custom implementation of the gRPC Server Reflection Protocol (`grpc.reflection.v1.ServerReflection`).
421	
422	### 2.1 The Immutability of `tonic-reflection`
423	
424	The standard `tonic_reflection::server::Builder` consumes registered `FileDescriptorSet`s and produces an immutable `ServerReflectionServer`. Internally, it indexes all files, services, messages, and enums into static `HashMap`s. There are no exposed APIs to mutate this state post-build. 
425	
426	Therefore, relying on the built-in `tonic-reflection` service is insufficient for dynamic plugin registration. Instead, the system must implement the reflection protocol manually, backed by a mutable store.
427	
428	## 3. Implementation Details
429	
430	### 3.1 Schema to Protobuf Type Mapping
431	
432	The declarative nature of JSON Schema must be mapped to the rigid, strongly-typed structure of Protocol Buffers. The following mapping strategy is recommended:
433	
434	| JSON Schema Type / Keyword | Protobuf Field Type / Construct | Notes |
435	| :--- | :--- | :--- |
436	| `string` | `TYPE_STRING` | Maps directly. |
437	| `integer` | `TYPE_INT64` | Default to 64-bit for maximum range. Use `format` hints for `TYPE_INT32`. |
438	| `number` | `TYPE_DOUBLE` | Default to double precision. Use `format` hints for `TYPE_FLOAT`. |
439	| `boolean` | `TYPE_BOOL` | Maps directly. |
440	| `array` | `LABEL_REPEATED` | The `items` keyword dictates the inner element type. |
441	| `object` | `TYPE_MESSAGE` | Translates to a nested `DescriptorProto`. |
442	| `null` / `nullable` | `optional` keyword | Mapped using proto3 `optional` presence. |
443	| `$ref` | `type_name` | Resolves to the fully qualified name of the referenced `DescriptorProto`. |
444	| `anyOf` / `oneOf` | `oneof` wrapper | Maps to a protobuf `oneof` group containing each variant. |
445	
446	**Stable Field Numbering:** Protobuf requires stable field numbers. Because JSON Schema properties are unordered, field numbers must be assigned deterministically. A common approach is to compute a stable hash (e.g., FNV-1a or CRC32) of the field name, modulo the maximum valid protobuf field number (536,870,911), ensuring the result avoids the reserved range (19000-29999).
447	
448	### 3.2 Programmatic Descriptor Synthesis
449	
450	Using `prost-types`, the system constructs the descriptor tree from the bottom up:
451	
452	1. **Messages:** Iterate over `$defs`. For each schema definition, create a `DescriptorProto`. Map its properties to `FieldDescriptorProto` entries using the mapping rules above.
453	2. **Services:** Extract `x-methods` from the schema. For each method, create a `MethodDescriptorProto`, specifying the fully qualified `input_type` and `output_type`.
454	3. **Files:** Wrap the messages and services in a `FileDescriptorProto`, assigning a unique package name (e.g., `plugin.v1.<plugin_id>`).
455	
456	```rust
457	use prost_types::{DescriptorProto, FieldDescriptorProto, FileDescriptorProto, MethodDescriptorProto, ServiceDescriptorProto};
458	
459	fn synthesize_plugin_descriptor(plugin_id: &str, schema: &schemars::schema::RootSchema) -> FileDescriptorProto {
460	    let mut file = FileDescriptorProto {
461	        name: Some(format!("{}.proto", plugin_id)),
462	        package: Some(format!("plugin.v1.{}", plugin_id)),
463	        syntax: Some("proto3".to_string()),
464	        ..Default::default()
465	    };
466	    
467	    // 1. Synthesize Messages from $defs
468	    // ... logic to convert schema.$defs to file.message_type ...
469	    
470	    // 2. Synthesize Service from x-methods
471	    // ... logic to convert custom methods extension to file.service ...
472	    
473	    file
474	}
475	```
476	
477	### 3.3 Dynamic Descriptor Pool Management
478	
479	The `prost-reflect` crate provides `DescriptorPool`, which manages dependencies and enables runtime introspection. The custom reflection service must maintain an `Arc<RwLock<DescriptorPool>>` to allow concurrent reads from reflection clients and exclusive writes during plugin registration.
480	
481	When a new plugin registers:
482	1. Synthesize its `FileDescriptorProto`.
483	2. Acquire a write lock on the `DescriptorPool`.
484	3. Call `pool.add_file_descriptor_proto(file_proto)`.
485	4. Release the lock.
486	
487	### 3.4 Custom Server Reflection Implementation
488	
489	To serve the dynamically updated pool, implement the `grpc.reflection.v1.ServerReflection` trait. The `ServerReflectionInfo` RPC is a bidirectional stream. The implementation must handle requests like `file_by_filename`, `file_containing_symbol`, and `list_services` by querying the shared `DescriptorPool`.
490	
491	```rust
492	use tonic::{Request, Response, Status, Streaming};
493	use tokio::sync::mpsc;
494	use std::sync::{Arc, RwLock};
495	use prost_reflect::DescriptorPool;
496	
497	// Import generated types from tonic-reflection or your own compiled protos
498	// use tonic_reflection::pb::v1::{ServerReflection, ServerReflectionRequest, ServerReflectionResponse};
499	
500	pub struct DynamicReflectionService {
501	    pool: Arc<RwLock<DescriptorPool>>,
502	}
503	
504	#[tonic::async_trait]
505	impl ServerReflection for DynamicReflectionService {
506	    type ServerReflectionInfoStream = tokio_stream::wrappers::ReceiverStream<Result<ServerReflectionResponse, Status>>;
507	
508	    async fn server_reflection_info(
509	        &self,
510	        request: Request<Streaming<ServerReflectionRequest>>,
511	    ) -> Result<Response<Self::ServerReflectionInfoStream>, Status> {
512	        let mut in_stream = request.into_inner();
513	        let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel(100);
514	        let pool_ref = self.pool.clone();
515	
516	        tokio::spawn(async move {
517	            while let Some(Ok(req)) = in_stream.message().await {
518	                let pool = pool_ref.read().unwrap();
519	                let response = match req.message_request {
520	                    Some(server_reflection_request::MessageRequest::ListServices(_)) => {
521	                        let services = pool.services()
522	                            .map(|s| ServiceResponse { name: s.full_name().to_string() })
523	                            .collect();
524	                        // Construct ListServicesResponse...
525	                    },
526	                    Some(server_reflection_request::MessageRequest::FileContainingSymbol(symbol)) => {
527	                        if let Some(file_desc) = pool.get_file_by_name(&symbol) {
528	                            let encoded = prost::Message::encode_to_vec(file_desc.file_descriptor_proto());
529	                            // Construct FileDescriptorResponse...
530	                        } else {
531	                            // Construct ErrorResponse (NOT_FOUND)...
532	                        }
533	                    },
534	                    // Handle other request types...
535	                    _ => { /* Construct ErrorResponse (UNIMPLEMENTED) */ }
536	                };
537	                if tx.send(Ok(response)).await.is_err() { break; }
538	            }
539	        });
540	
541	        Ok(Response::new(tokio_stream::wrappers::ReceiverStream::new(rx)))
542	    }
543	}
544	```
545	
546	### 3.5 Dynamic Routing for Method Invocations
547	
548	While reflection allows clients to *discover* the services, the `tonic` server must also be able to *route* incoming gRPC requests to the correct plugin implementation.
549	
550	Because the services are not known at compile time, they cannot be added via `tonic::transport::Server::add_service`. Instead, a custom `tower::Service` acting as a dynamic router must be placed in front of the server, or implemented as a fallback.
551	
552	This router intercepts `http::Request<Body>`, inspects the URI path (e.g., `/plugin.v1.MyPlugin/MyMethod`), decodes the incoming protobuf bytes using `prost_reflect::DynamicMessage`, translates the payload to a D-Bus method call (via `zbus` or `dbus-rs`), and encodes the D-Bus response back to protobuf bytes.
553	
554	## 4. Known Limitations and Pitfalls
555	
556	*   **Field Number Collisions:** If stable hashing is not used for field numbers, or if the hash algorithm produces collisions, the generated descriptors will be invalid or incompatible across schema reloads.
557	*   **Dependency Resolution:** The `DescriptorPool` must be initialized with well-known types (e.g., `google/protobuf/any.proto`, `google/protobuf/empty.proto`) before dynamically synthesized descriptors that reference them can be added.
558	*   **Concurrency Overhead:** The `RwLock` around the `DescriptorPool` introduces a potential bottleneck if plugin registration/deregistration is highly frequent, though reads (reflection queries) are highly concurrent.
559	*   **Schema Validation:** Malformed `schemars` definitions (e.g., missing `$ref` targets) must be gracefully handled during descriptor synthesis to prevent the reflection service from crashing.
560	
561	## 5. Conclusion
562	
563	By combining `prost-types` for programmatic descriptor construction, `prost-reflect` for runtime pool management, and a custom implementation of the gRPC Server Reflection Protocol, the system can successfully synthesize and serve dynamic gRPC reflection for schema-projected D-Bus services. This approach completely bypasses the limitations of the static `tonic-reflection` builder, enabling a truly dynamic, schema-driven plugin architecture.

588	## 2. Encoding Methods in `schemars`
589	
590	To generate gRPC methods, the JSON Schema must contain method signatures. The recommended approach is to use the `schemars` `schema_with` attribute or a custom schema generator to inject an `x-methods` extension into the `RootSchema`.
591	
592	### 2.1 The `x-methods` Convention
593	
594	The `x-methods` extension should be a structured array of method definitions:
595	
596	```json
597	{
598	  "type": "object",
599	  "properties": { ... },
600	  "x-methods": [
601	    {
602	      "name": "ProcessData",
603	      "args": {
604	        "input_string": { "type": "string" },
605	        "count": { "type": "integer" }
606	      },
607	      "returns": { "$ref": "#/$defs/ProcessResult" }
608	    }
609	  ]
610	}
611	```
612	
613	### 2.2 Generating the Schema in Rust
614	
615	You can manually inject this during schema generation:
616	
617	```rust
618	use schemars::{gen::SchemaGenerator, schema::{Schema, SchemaObject}, JsonSchema};
619	
620	#[derive(JsonSchema)]
621	pub struct MyPluginData {
622	    pub status: String,
623	}
624	
625	pub fn generate_plugin_schema() -> schemars::schema::RootSchema {
626	    let mut gen = SchemaGenerator::default();
627	    let mut schema = gen.root_schema_for::<MyPluginData>();
628	    
629	    let methods = serde_json::json!([
630	        {
631	            "name": "ProcessData",
632	            "args": { "input": { "type": "string" } },
633	            "returns": { "type": "string" }
634	        }
635	    ]);
636	    
637	    schema.schema.extensions.insert("x-methods".to_string(), methods);
638	    schema
639	}
640	```

642	## 3. Programmatic `FileDescriptorProto` Construction
643	
644	At object instantiation time, the system parses the `RootSchema` and synthesizes a `prost_types::FileDescriptorProto`.
645	
646	### 3.1 Mapping Rules
647	
648	| JSON Schema | Protobuf `prost_types::field_descriptor_proto::Type` |
649	| :--- | :--- |
650	| `string` | `Type::String` |
651	| `integer` | `Type::Int64` |
652	| `number` | `Type::Double` |
653	| `boolean` | `Type::Bool` |
654	| `array` | Set `label` to `Label::Repeated` |
655	| `$ref` | `Type::Message`, set `type_name` to fully qualified name |
656	
657	### 3.2 Construction Example
658	
659	```rust
660	use prost_types::{
661	    field_descriptor_proto::{Label, Type},
662	    DescriptorProto, FieldDescriptorProto, FileDescriptorProto, MethodDescriptorProto, ServiceDescriptorProto,
663	};
664	
665	pub fn synthesize_descriptor(plugin_id: &str, schema: &schemars::schema::RootSchema) -> FileDescriptorProto {
666	    let mut file = FileDescriptorProto::default();
667	    file.name = Some(format!("{}.proto", plugin_id));
668	    file.package = Some(format!("plugin.v1.{}", plugin_id));
669	    file.syntax = Some("proto3".to_string());
670	
671	    // 1. Convert $defs to message types
672	    // ... logic to map schema definitions to file.message_type ...
673	
674	    // 2. Extract x-methods to ServiceDescriptorProto
675	    let mut service = ServiceDescriptorProto::default();
676	    service.name = Some(format!("{}Service", plugin_id));
677	
678	    if let Some(methods_val) = schema.schema.extensions.get("x-methods") {
679	        if let Some(methods_arr) = methods_val.as_array() {
680	            for method_val in methods_arr {
681	                // For each method, synthesize Request and Response messages
682	                let method_name = method_val["name"].as_str().unwrap();
683	                let req_name = format!("{}Request", method_name);
684	                let res_name = format!("{}Response", method_name);
685	
686	                // ... synthesize DescriptorProto for req_name and res_name, add to file.message_type ...
687	
688	                let mut method = MethodDescriptorProto::default();
689	                method.name = Some(method_name.to_string());
690	                method.input_type = Some(format!(".plugin.v1.{}.{}", plugin_id, req_name));
691	                method.output_type = Some(format!(".plugin.v1.{}.{}", plugin_id, res_name));
692	                
693	                service.method.push(method);
694	            }
695	        }
696	    }
697	
698	    file.service.push(service);
699	    file
700	}
701	```

703	## 4. Coupling the Descriptor to the D-Bus Object
704	
705	The generated descriptor is a permanent, immutable artifact tied to the D-Bus object. It should be cached to avoid redundant generation for objects sharing the same schema.
706	
707	### 4.1 The `GrpcDescriptor` Trait
708	
709	```rust
710	use bytes::Bytes;
711	use std::sync::Arc;
712	
713	pub trait GrpcDescriptor {
714	    /// Returns the encoded FileDescriptorSet bytes for reflection
715	    fn get_descriptor_bytes(&self) -> Arc<Bytes>;
716	    /// Returns the fully qualified gRPC service name
717	    fn get_service_name(&self) -> &str;
718	}
719	```
720	
721	### 4.2 Caching and Struct Definition
722	
723	```rust
724	use once_cell::sync::Lazy;
725	use std::collections::HashMap;
726	use std::sync::Mutex;
727	
728	pub struct CachedDescriptor {
729	    pub file_descriptor_set_bytes: Arc<Bytes>,
730	    pub service_name: String,
731	}
732	
733	pub static DESCRIPTOR_CACHE: Lazy<Mutex<HashMap<String, Arc<CachedDescriptor>>>> = Lazy::new(|| {
734	    Mutex::new(HashMap::new())
735	});
736	
737	pub struct DbusPluginObject {
738	    pub object_path: String,
739	    pub descriptor: Arc<CachedDescriptor>,
740	}
741	
742	impl GrpcDescriptor for DbusPluginObject {
743	    fn get_descriptor_bytes(&self) -> Arc<Bytes> {
744	        Arc::clone(&self.descriptor.file_descriptor_set_bytes)
745	    }
746	    fn get_service_name(&self) -> &str {
747	        &self.descriptor.service_name
748	    }
749	}
750	```
751	
752	At instantiation, check the `DESCRIPTOR_CACHE` using the schema's hash. If absent, synthesize the `FileDescriptorProto`, wrap it in a `FileDescriptorSet`, encode it using `prost::Message::encode_to_vec()`, and store the `Bytes` in the cache.
753	
754	## 5. Integrating with `prost-reflect` and `tonic`
755	
756	### 5.1 Global Descriptor Pool
757	
758	Maintain a global `prost_reflect::DescriptorPool` initialized with well-known types:
759	
760	```rust
761	use prost_reflect::DescriptorPool;
762	
763	pub static GLOBAL_POOL: Lazy<std::sync::RwLock<DescriptorPool>> = Lazy::new(|| {
764	    let mut pool = DescriptorPool::new();
765	    // Add well-known types
766	    pool.add_file_descriptor_set(prost_reflect::well_known_types::FILE_DESCRIPTOR_SET).unwrap();
767	    std::sync::RwLock::new(pool)
768	});
769	```
770	
771	When a D-Bus object is instantiated, add its synthesized `FileDescriptorSet` to this global pool:
772	
773	```rust
774	GLOBAL_POOL.write().unwrap().add_file_descriptor_set(decoded_set).unwrap();
775	```
776	
777	### 5.2 Custom Reflection Service
778	
779	As established, `tonic-reflection`'s builder is static. You must implement `grpc.reflection.v1.ServerReflection` manually. The implementation reads from `GLOBAL_POOL` to answer `file_by_filename` and `file_containing_symbol` requests, ensuring that the reflection data served exactly matches the locked-in descriptors of the currently active D-Bus objects.
780

Notes on using grpc with rust and tonic
In the Tonic examples proto files are used to generated service and client stubs with tonic_build.

The Getting started section mentions the following:

For IntelliJ IDEA users, please refer to this and enable org.rust.cargo.evaluate.build.scripts experimental feature.

But in order to have a nice development experience you need some additional tweaks.

You can find the full code here: https://github.com/timvw/arrow-flightsql-odbc

By default the stubs are generated in ./target/…/build/… Unfortunately CLion does not scan those folders and you don’t get to benefit from intellisense.

As a workaround you can generate the stubs in your ./src folder instead. You can do that by configuring the tonic_build in build.rs.

While you are at it, you should also enable the writing of a file_descriptor_set to enable GRPC Server Reflection using tonic-reflection.

build.rs
use std::env;
use std::path::PathBuf;

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {

    //intellij does not easily find types when not adding code to src
    //tonic_build::compile_protos("proto/Flight.proto")?;
    //tonic_build::compile_protos("proto/FlightSql.proto")?;

    let original_out_dir = PathBuf::from(env::var("OUT_DIR")?);

    let out_dir = "./src";

    tonic_build::configure()
        .out_dir(out_dir)
        .file_descriptor_set_path(original_out_dir.join("flight_descriptor.bin"))
        .compile(&["proto/Flight.proto"], &["proto"])?;

    tonic_build::configure()
        .out_dir(out_dir)
        .file_descriptor_set_path(original_out_dir.join("flight_sql_descriptor.bin"))
        .compile(&["proto/FlightSql.proto"], &["proto"])?;

    Ok(())
}
Now you can update your lib.rs and include the generated stubs by referring to their path in ./src instead of the include_proto! macro. Notice that I have also used the include_file_descriptor_set to enable the GRPC Server Reflection:

src/lib.rs
/*
pub mod arrow_flight_protocol {
    tonic::include_proto!("arrow.flight.protocol"); // The string specified here must match the proto package name
}

pub mod arrow_flight_protocol_sql {
    tonic::include_proto!("arrow.flight.protocol.sql"); // The string specified here must match the proto package name
}
 */

#[path = "arrow.flight.protocol.rs"]
pub mod arrow_flight_protocol;

#[path = "arrow.flight.protocol.sql.rs"]
pub mod arrow_flight_protocol_sql;

pub const FLIGHT_DESCRIPTOR_SET: &[u8] = tonic::include_file_descriptor_set!("flight_descriptor");
pub const FLIGHT_SQL_DESCRIPTOR_SET: &[u8] = tonic::include_file_descriptor_set!("flight_sql_descriptor");
Now you can create your server and register the reflection service:

src/bin/server.rs
let reflection_server = tonic_reflection::server::Builder::configure()
    .register_encoded_file_descriptor_set(arrow_flightsql_odbc::FLIGHT_DESCRIPTOR_SET)
    .register_encoded_file_descriptor_set(arrow_flightsql_odbc::FLIGHT_SQL_DESCRIPTOR_SET)
    .build()?;

Server::builder()
    .add_service(FlightServiceServer::new(myserver))
    .add_service(reflection_server)
    .serve(addr)
    .await?;
