---
name: project_s6_commit_prune_hazard
description: "s6-frontend `s6 set commit` prunes the live-referenced compiled db, dangling bootdb; safe recovery procedure"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: baf4e3ab-78a3-4629-beb2-c492ee37aa7b
---

On this Artix box, `s6 set commit` (s6-frontend) compiles a new db AND garbage-collects the old compiled db **even though `/etc/s6/rc/compiled` (the `bootdb` per `s6-frontend.conf`) still hardlinks it by full path**. If `s6 live install` doesn't immediately follow (e.g. it fails on a lock), you're left with: dangling `bootdb` (reboot can fail), and `/run/s6-rc/state` keyed to the now-gone db so `s6-rc` reports "unable to read valid state". Running services are UNAFFECTED — s6-svscan supervises them independently; only the s6-rc management/boot layer breaks.

**Always do `s6 set commit` and `s6 live install` back-to-back.** The window between them is the hazard. Use `sudo s6-apply` (`/usr/local/bin/s6-apply`) — the wrapper that does sync→commit→live install atomically, keeps bootdb synced to the live db, rolls bootdb back on failure, and verifies state read afterward. Don't run `s6 set commit` by hand. (The individual `s6` subcommands can't be removed — they're built into the frontend binary — so s6-apply is convention, not enforcement.)

**Recovery when the old db is already pruned (validated, no service disruption):**
1. Preserve the new db to a stable path outside `/etc/s6/repo/compiled` gc scope: `cp -a <repo/compiled/current> /etc/s6/manualdb/<name>`.
2. Reconstruct an old-equiv db: `s6 set mask <newsvcs>` (NOT `disable` — disable keeps them in the db; only `mask` removes from db) → `s6 set commit`. Deterministic compile reproduces the lost db's numbering.
3. Point `/etc/s6/rc/compiled` -> old-equiv. READ-ONLY VALIDATE: `s6-rc -a list` must read state AND up/down must match ground truth (`s6-svstat` each `/run/s6-rc/servicedirs/*`). Mismatch → abort.
4. Dry-run `s6-rc-update -n -v2 -l /run/s6-rc <preserved-new-db>` — confirm stop-list and start-list are EMPTY (no disruption), then run for real.
5. Point `bootdb` -> preserved new db. Reconcile frontend: `s6 set unmask` + `s6 set enable` + `s6 set commit`.

Keeping boot/live on the stable `/etc/s6/manualdb` copy (not `repo/compiled/current`) makes it immune to future commit gc. See [[artix-s6-layout]]. New service installed this way: zeroclaw-gui-srv/-log (see [[project_zeroclaw_gui_service]]).

9	
10	# Artix Linux S6 Layout
11	
12	This host runs **Artix Linux** with s6-rc. Service sources live in `/etc/s6/sv/`, compiled DB at `/etc/s6/rc/compiled`.
13	
14	## Canonical workflow for adding a new service
15	
16	### 1. Create source files in the deploy tree (git-tracked)
17	
18	```
19	deploy/s6/op-<name>-srv/
20	  run              — executable sh script, use `exec s6-setuidgid jeremy /usr/local/bin/<binary>`
21	  type             — contains "longrun"
22	  notification-fd  — contains "3"
23	  producer-for     — contains "op-<name>-log"
24	  dependencies.d/
25	    dbus-session   — empty file (dependency)
26	    op-cognitive-mcp — empty file (if needs memory)
27	
28	deploy/s6/op-<name>-log/
29	  run              — execlineb logger script (see template below)
30	  type             — contains "longrun"
31	  notification-fd  — contains "3"
32	  consumer-for     — contains "op-<name>-srv"
33	  pipeline-name    — contains "op-<name>"
34	```
35	
36	### 2. Logger run script template (execlineb)
37	
38	```
39	#!/bin/execlineb -P
40	envfile -I /etc/s6/config/op-<name>.conf
41	importas -sCuD "n5 s2000000 T" DIRECTIVES DIRECTIVES
42	ifelse { test -w /var/log } {
43		foreground { install -d -o s6log -g s6log /var/log/op-<name> }
44		s6-setuidgid s6log exec -c s6-log -d3 -b -- ${DIRECTIVES} /var/log/op-<name>
45	}
46	foreground { install -d -o s6log -g s6log /run/log/op-<name> }
47	s6-setuidgid s6log exec -c s6-log -d3 -b -- ${DIRECTIVES} /run/log/op-<name>
48	```
49	
50	Requires an empty conf file: `sudo touch /etc/s6/config/op-<name>.conf`
51	
52	### 3. Copy to live system
53	
54	```bash
55	sudo cp -r deploy/s6/op-<name>-srv /etc/s6/sv/
56	sudo cp -r deploy/s6/op-<name>-log /etc/s6/sv/
57	```
58	
59	### 4. Register in the s6 frontend source tree
60	
61	New services need symlinks in the `active/` and `usable/` source directories:
62	
63	```bash
64	for svc in op-<name>-srv op-<name>-log; do
65	  sudo ln -sf "../../.atomics/${svc}" "/etc/s6/repo/sources/current/active/${svc}"
66	done
67	sudo ln -sf "../../.atomics/op-<name>-srv" "/etc/s6/repo/sources/current/usable/op-<name>-srv"
68	```
69	
70	Also add to a bundle's `contents.d/`:
71	```bash
72	sudo touch /etc/s6/sv/misc/contents.d/op-<name>-srv
73	```
74	
75	### 5. Compile and install (when .ref rebuild works)
76	
77	```bash
78	sudo s6 set commit --default-bundle=system-default
79	sudo s6 live install
80	sudo s6 live start op-<name>-srv
81	```
82	
83	**Current blocker:** `s6 set commit` fails with `rpcbind-srv is not a valid identifier in .ref` when adding services not yet in the compiled `.ref` database. The `.ref` at `/etc/s6/repo/compiled/.ref` needs a full rebuild. Workaround: add startup to `rc-local/up`.
84	
85	## Enable an EXISTING service for boot (persistence)
86	
87	If `s6 set status` shows a service as `<name>/usable` (available but NOT enabled), it is absent from the `default` boot bundle and won't auto-start. To make it persistent:
88	
89	```bash
90	sudo s6 set enable op-<name>          # usable -> active in working set
91	sudo sh deploy/s6/recompile-and-update.sh   # commits + s6 live install, preserves `default` bundle
92	sudo s6 live start op-<name>          # live install resets servicedir; start it now
93	```
94	
95	Verify: `s6-rc-db -c /run/s6-rc/compiled all-dependencies default | grep op-<name>` (in boot tree), and `s6-svstat` shows `up` WITHOUT "normally down" (the "normally down" suffix means a stale `down` flag / not enabled). `recompile-and-update.sh` worked cleanly on 2026-06-19 — it's the canonical commit+install path; do NOT hand-run `s6 set commit`/`s6-rc-db` directly.
96	
97	## Changing an existing service's env (e.g. a key in `/etc/s6/sv/<name>/env/`)
98	
99	Editing `/etc/s6/sv/<name>/env/VAR` then `s6-svc -r` does **NOT** apply it: the run script does `s6-envdir ./env` relative to the **live** servicedir `/run/s6-rc/servicedirs/<name>` (a frozen copy installed at boot, tmpfs), not `/etc/s6/sv`. You must recompile→install:
100	```bash
101	sudo s6 repository sync          # pull /etc/s6/sv edits into repo sources
102	sudo s6 set check -F -u
103	sudo s6 set commit -f -D default # -D default = avoids "bundle default already defined"
104	new_db="$(sudo readlink -f /etc/s6/repo/compiled/current)"
105	sudo s6 live install -b          # swaps live servicedirs (regenerated from source)
106	sudo ln -sfnT "$new_db" /etc/s6/rc/compiled   # repoint bootdb for REBOOT persistence
107	```
108	This is exactly what `deploy/s6/recompile-and-update.sh` automates (run with `SKIP_BUILD=1` to skip the cargo rebuild for env-only changes). `/etc/s6/sv` = persistent source; `/etc/s6/rc/compiled` symlink = what boot loads; `/run/s6-rc` = live tmpfs copy.
109	
110	## BOOT WEDGE: `op-web-srv` holds the global s6-rc lock (2026-06-20)
111	
112	`op-web-srv` is a `longrun` with `notification-fd=3` (s6 waits for a readiness notify). `op-web-server` starts but never binds `:8080` and never notifies ready (stuck in init — likely can't reach `OP_DBUS_GRPC_ADDR=http://10.200.0.1:50051` or dbus-session). So at boot `s6-rc -up change default` (pid ~298) blocks forever on `s6-svlisten -U -- op-web-srv`, **holding the global s6-rc lock**. Effect: every `s6 live install` / `s6-rc-update` **hangs** (use a `timeout`; don't trust `-b`). Unrelated services still come up — op-cognitive-mcp (deps: only `dbus-session`, no readiness gate) is up despite the wedge. This is SIGNALS OD-23. Do NOT force-kill pid 298 lightly (global lock → cascade risk; cf. [[project_incus_boot_wedge]]). See [[project_cognitive_grpc_endpoint]].
113	
114	**ROOT CAUSE + FIX (staged 2026-06-20):** `op-web-srv` AND `op-assistant-grpc-srv` declared `notification-fd=3` but their Rust binaries implement **no s6 readiness** (no `sd_notify`/fd-3 write) — so `s6-svlisten -U` waits forever. (`dbus-srv` also has nfd=3 but genuinely signals `ready`, so it's fine — don't touch it.) Fix = removed the `notification-fd` file from both services in the live store `/etc/s6/sv/` AND git source `deploy/s6/`, recompiled (`s6 repository sync` → `s6 set commit -f -D default`), repointed bootdb. Effect: those services are marked up immediately on exec, the boot transition completes, lock releases — no wedge. **Applies on next reboot** (live install was lock-blocked; uncommitted git deletions of the two `notification-fd` files remain). General rule: never set `notification-fd` on a service whose binary doesn't write the readiness byte — it wedges boot and holds the global s6-rc lock.
115	
116	## Key paths
117	
118	| Path | Purpose |
119	|------|---------|

---
name: artix-s6-layout
description: "Artix Linux s6 service layout — exact structure for adding services, canonical deploy script"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 530852a9-02e8-4af8-bdf1-8d45b02180a7
---

# Artix Linux S6 Layout

This host runs **Artix Linux** with s6-rc. Service sources live in `/etc/s6/sv/`, compiled DB at `/etc/s6/rc/compiled`.

## Canonical workflow for adding a new service

### 1. Create source files in the deploy tree (git-tracked)

```
deploy/s6/op-<name>-srv/
  run              — executable sh script, use `exec s6-setuidgid jeremy /usr/local/bin/<binary>`
  type             — contains "longrun"
  notification-fd  — contains "3"
  producer-for     — contains "op-<name>-log"
  dependencies.d/
    dbus-session   — empty file (dependency)
    op-cognitive-mcp — empty file (if needs memory)

deploy/s6/op-<name>-log/
  run              — execlineb logger script (see template below)
  type             — contains "longrun"
  notification-fd  — contains "3"
  consumer-for     — contains "op-<name>-srv"
  pipeline-name    — contains "op-<name>"
```

### 2. Logger run script template (execlineb)

```
#!/bin/execlineb -P
envfile -I /etc/s6/config/op-<name>.conf
importas -sCuD "n5 s2000000 T" DIRECTIVES DIRECTIVES
ifelse { test -w /var/log } {
	foreground { install -d -o s6log -g s6log /var/log/op-<name> }
	s6-setuidgid s6log exec -c s6-log -d3 -b -- ${DIRECTIVES} /var/log/op-<name>
}
foreground { install -d -o s6log -g s6log /run/log/op-<name> }
s6-setuidgid s6log exec -c s6-log -d3 -b -- ${DIRECTIVES} /run/log/op-<name>
```

Requires an empty conf file: `sudo touch /etc/s6/config/op-<name>.conf`

### 3. Copy to live system

```bash
sudo cp -r deploy/s6/op-<name>-srv /etc/s6/sv/
sudo cp -r deploy/s6/op-<name>-log /etc/s6/sv/
```

### 4. Register in the s6 frontend source tree

New services need symlinks in the `active/` and `usable/` source directories:

```bash
for svc in op-<name>-srv op-<name>-log; do
  sudo ln -sf "../../.atomics/${svc}" "/etc/s6/repo/sources/current/active/${svc}"
done
sudo ln -sf "../../.atomics/op-<name>-srv" "/etc/s6/repo/sources/current/usable/op-<name>-srv"
```

Also add to a bundle's `contents.d/`:
```bash
sudo touch /etc/s6/sv/misc/contents.d/op-<name>-srv
```

### 5. Compile and install (when .ref rebuild works)

```bash
sudo s6 set commit --default-bundle=system-default
sudo s6 live install
sudo s6 live start op-<name>-srv
```

**Current blocker:** `s6 set commit` fails with `rpcbind-srv is not a valid identifier in .ref` when adding services not yet in the compiled `.ref` database. The `.ref` at `/etc/s6/repo/compiled/.ref` needs a full rebuild. Workaround: add startup to `rc-local/up`.

## Enable an EXISTING service for boot (persistence)

If `s6 set status` shows a service as `<name>/usable` (available but NOT enabled), it is absent from the `default` boot bundle and won't auto-start. To make it persistent:

```bash
sudo s6 set enable op-<name>          # usable -> active in working set
sudo sh deploy/s6/recompile-and-update.sh   # commits + s6 live install, preserves `default` bundle
sudo s6 live start op-<name>          # live install resets servicedir; start it now
```

Verify: `s6-rc-db -c /run/s6-rc/compiled all-dependencies default | grep op-<name>` (in boot tree), and `s6-svstat` shows `up` WITHOUT "normally down" (the "normally down" suffix means a stale `down` flag / not enabled). `recompile-and-update.sh` worked cleanly on 2026-06-19 — it's the canonical commit+install path; do NOT hand-run `s6 set commit`/`s6-rc-db` directly.

## Changing an existing service's env (e.g. a key in `/etc/s6/sv/<name>/env/`)

Editing `/etc/s6/sv/<name>/env/VAR` then `s6-svc -r` does **NOT** apply it: the run script does `s6-envdir ./env` relative to the **live** servicedir `/run/s6-rc/servicedirs/<name>` (a frozen copy installed at boot, tmpfs), not `/etc/s6/sv`. You must recompile→install:
```bash
sudo s6 repository sync          # pull /etc/s6/sv edits into repo sources
sudo s6 set check -F -u
sudo s6 set commit -f -D default # -D default = avoids "bundle default already defined"
new_db="$(sudo readlink -f /etc/s6/repo/compiled/current)"
sudo s6 live install -b          # swaps live servicedirs (regenerated from source)
sudo ln -sfnT "$new_db" /etc/s6/rc/compiled   # repoint bootdb for REBOOT persistence
```
This is exactly what `deploy/s6/recompile-and-update.sh` automates (run with `SKIP_BUILD=1` to skip the cargo rebuild for env-only changes). `/etc/s6/sv` = persistent source; `/etc/s6/rc/compiled` symlink = what boot loads; `/run/s6-rc` = live tmpfs copy.

## BOOT WEDGE: `op-web-srv` holds the global s6-rc lock (2026-06-20)

`op-web-srv` is a `longrun` with `notification-fd=3` (s6 waits for a readiness notify). `op-web-server` starts but never binds `:8080` and never notifies ready (stuck in init — likely can't reach `OP_DBUS_GRPC_ADDR=http://10.200.0.1:50051` or dbus-session). So at boot `s6-rc -up change default` (pid ~298) blocks forever on `s6-svlisten -U -- op-web-srv`, **holding the global s6-rc lock**. Effect: every `s6 live install` / `s6-rc-update` **hangs** (use a `timeout`; don't trust `-b`). Unrelated services still come up — op-cognitive-mcp (deps: only `dbus-session`, no readiness gate) is up despite the wedge. This is SIGNALS OD-23. Do NOT force-kill pid 298 lightly (global lock → cascade risk; cf. [[project_incus_boot_wedge]]). See [[project_cognitive_grpc_endpoint]].

**ROOT CAUSE + FIX (staged 2026-06-20):** `op-web-srv` AND `op-assistant-grpc-srv` declared `notification-fd=3` but their Rust binaries implement **no s6 readiness** (no `sd_notify`/fd-3 write) — so `s6-svlisten -U` waits forever. (`dbus-srv` also has nfd=3 but genuinely signals `ready`, so it's fine — don't touch it.) Fix = removed the `notification-fd` file from both services in the live store `/etc/s6/sv/` AND git source `deploy/s6/`, recompiled (`s6 repository sync` → `s6 set commit -f -D default`), repointed bootdb. Effect: those services are marked up immediately on exec, the boot transition completes, lock releases — no wedge. **Applies on next reboot** (live install was lock-blocked; uncommitted git deletions of the two `notification-fd` files remain). General rule: never set `notification-fd` on a service whose binary doesn't write the readiness byte — it wedges boot and holds the global s6-rc lock.

## Key paths

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `/etc/s6/sv/` | Live service source definitions (= `.atomics/` symlink target) |
| `/etc/s6/repo/compiled/current` | Active compiled s6-rc DB |
| `/etc/s6/repo/compiled/.ref` | Working-set reference DB (separate from live) |
| `/etc/s6/repo/sources/current/active/` | Symlinks to services included in compilation |
| `/etc/s6/repo/sources/current/usable/` | Symlinks to services enabled at boot |
| `/etc/s6/repo/stores/0000/` | Store 0 = mirrors `/etc/s6/sv/` service dirs |
| `/etc/s6/repo/stores/0001/` | Store 1 = extra services (mount-filesystems, network) |
| `/etc/s6/config/*.conf` | Logger directive files (can be empty) |

## Do NOT use

- `s6 set commit` without `--default-bundle` — fails with "bundle default already defined"
- Manual symlinks into `/run/service/` — wrong approach, s6-svscan manages that
- `pipeline-name` file value must NOT match the service directory name — causes duplicate definition compile error

## Environment variables in run scripts

Use `export VAR="${VAR:-default}"` pattern. For secrets, use `/etc/s6/sv/<name>/env/` directory (one file per variable, filename = var name, file content = value), accessed via `exec s6-envdir ./env ...` or `s6-setuidgid`.

content.text:
## Full findings from the log/health sweep

**Boot itself: healthy.** Kernel came up clean aside from two minor dmesg items; all core services (`dbus-session`, `op-cognitive-mcp`, `op-dbus-mirror`, `op-projection`, `ovs-vswitchd`, `incus`, `op-web-srv`) are up and stable.

**Two minor, non-blocking items:**
1. `FAT-fs (sda1): Volume was not properly unmounted` — from the earlier abrupt reboot during the outage. Worth an `fsck` on sda1 when convenient, not urgent.
2. `tmpfs: Unknown parameter 'none'` (x2) — cosmetic mount-option warning.

**Real, confirmed chain of failures (exactly matching your "xray down due to gemma" diagnosis) — now fixed for this boot:**
1. `gemma`'s oneshot `up` script has a genuine bug: it wraps `shell_up` in an execline `foreground {}` block but then unconditionally runs `exit 0` after — so even when `shell_up` fails (it has `set -eu` and would stop correctly on a real failure), s6 never sees that failure. #!/bin/sh
# s6-apply — the ONE safe way to push s6-frontend working-set changes live.
#
# Why this exists: `s6 set commit` compiles a new db AND garbage-collects the
# old one. If `s6 live install` does not immediately follow, the live-referenced
# compiled db can vanish, dangling the bootdb and breaking /run/s6-rc state
# (services keep running, but s6-rc management + next boot break). This wrapper
# performs sync -> commit -> live install back-to-back, keeps the bootdb in sync
# with the live db, and on any failure restores the bootdb so boot stays safe.
#
# Run this instead of `s6 set commit` / `s6 live install` by hand.
set -eu

log()  { printf '[s6-apply] %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die()  { log "FATAL: $*"; exit 1; }

[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || die "must run as root (try: sudo s6-apply)"

bootdb=/etc/s6/rc/compiled

# Remember the db the live system is currently on, so we can keep boot safe
# if the transition fails partway.
live_before=$(readlink -f /run/s6-rc/compiled 2>/dev/null || true)
[ -n "$live_before" ] && [ -d "$live_before" ] \
    || die "cannot resolve current live db (/run/s6-rc/compiled); refusing to proceed"
log "current live db: $live_before"

# 1. Pull any new/removed service defs from the stores into the working set.
log "syncing repository with stores"
s6 repository sync || die "repository sync failed (nothing changed)"

# 2. Compile the working set. After this point the old repo db may be pruned,
#    so step 3 MUST run — that is the whole reason for this wrapper.
log "committing working set"
s6 set commit || die "commit failed (nothing installed; live db untouched)"

# 3. Transition the live system onto the committed set.
if ! s6 live install -b; then
    log "live install failed — restoring bootdb to keep boot safe"
    ln -sfn "$live_before" "$bootdb"
    die "live install failed; live db left on $live_before. Investigate before retrying."
fi

# 4. Keep the bootdb pointed at exactly what the live system now runs, so the
#    next boot matches the running set.
live_after=$(readlink -f /run/s6-rc/compiled)
ln -sfn "$live_after" "$bootdb"

# 5. Sanity: s6-rc must be able to read live state against the new db.
s6-rc -a list >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "post-install s6-rc state read failed — DO NOT REBOOT, investigate"

log "ok. live + bootdb -> $live_after"

Unlike the D-Bus `daemon_reload` path (which has no rollback safety net and is likely what caused the earlier break), this one restores `bootdb` automatically if anything fails, and explicitly warns "DO NOT REBOOT" if the post-install check fails. Running it now.

This matches the documented wedge exactly. **`s6-apply` has been running 283 seconds and appears stuck** — `op-web-srv` shows `up (pid 20608) 282 seconds, normally down`, meaning a service that's *supposed* to stay down is up and, per my notes on this exact pattern, likely means s6 is blocked on `s6-svlisten -U` waiting for a readiness notification that will never arrive (this service's binary doesn't implement s6 readiness). That would hold the global s6-rc lock, explaining why `s6-apply` hasn't progressed past the ovsbr0 messages.

**Critical wrinkle**: my earlier bootdb-symlink fix only repointed the *boot* pointer at the old Jun 20 snapshot — it never touched the live `/etc/s6/sv/op-web-srv` source files. Today's `s6-apply` compiles fresh from whatever's currently in those source files, so the Jun 20 fix (removing `notification-fd` from `op-web-srv`) may not actually be present in the *current* source tree — meaning this wedge could be a genuine recurrence, not a fluke.

Per your instruction and my own notes ("do NOT force-kill lightly — global lock → cascade risk"), I'm stopping here rather than killing anything. **Not rebooting.** Status: `s6-apply` (pid 20410) still alive, no further log output for ~4+ minutes, `op-web-srv` up when it shouldn't be. Waiting for your read on how to proceed — options would be: wait longer in case it's just slow, check/fix `op-web-srv`'s source notification-fd file and let the commit retry, or carefully interrupt just the stuck `s6-svlisten` step (not the whole `s6-apply` process) if there's a clean way to do that. # S6 Boot Recovery + Gemma/Ollama Bring-Up — Handoff

Date: 2026-07-02
Host: `3tched` (Artix Linux, s6-rc)

## What happened, in order

1. **Original goal**: bring the `gemma4:12b` LLM up via zeroclaw's Ollama provider, and separately get the `gemma` s6 oneshot (xray/OpenFlow config generator) running.
2. While chasing a stale `op-s6-systemctl` D-Bus daemon (see below), a `daemon_reload` D-Bus call ran `s6 set commit` (which compiled a new db and garbage-collected the old one) but the client connection died before `s6 live install` could run and repoint `/etc/s6/rc/compiled` (bootdb). This left bootdb dangling at a deleted target — **the system became unbootable.**
3. Recovered via live rescue media + chroot into `/dev/sda3`. Repointed `/etc/s6/rc/compiled` to the last known-stable pre-incident compiled db (`.current:@400000006a369bdb346d3c96:YESXfi`, dated Jun 20 — validated to have both `default`/`boot` bundles and to be the specific post-fix db from the documented Jun 20 `op-web-srv` notification-fd wedge fix). Verified with `s6-rc-db check` (exit 0). **Reboot succeeded.**

## Root causes found and fixed

- **`op-s6-systemctl`'s `S6D_RELOAD_SCRIPT` env var defaults to `/usr/local/sbin/op-s6-recompile-and-update`, checked *before* the correct repo-path fallback** (`crates/op-s6-systemctl/src/dbus.rs::run_artix_frontend_reload`, ~line 139). A stale installed copy at that path existed and was self-referentially broken: it computes `PROJECT_ROOT` from its own `$0`, so when run from `/usr/local/sbin/...` it resolves to `/usr` instead of the real repo root — explaining both `find: 'target/release': No such file or directory` and `install: cannot stat '/usr/deploy/s6/recompile-and-update.sh'`. **Fixed**: deleted `/usr/local/sbin/op-s6-recompile-and-update`, forcing fallback to the correct repo script. This is a workaround, not a permanent code fix — the daemon's env-var precedence logic itself is still there and would recreate this exact bug if that path ever gets reinstalled (e.g. by a future `recompile-and-update.sh` run, since `install_control_scripts()` writes to that same path).
- **`op-s6-systemctl`'s running process was orphaned** — a child of PID 1 directly, not tracked by any current s6 servicedir I could find (killed it by mistake chasing a bad CWD-based assumption about which servicedir owned it — no collateral damage, but had to manually relaunch `/usr/local/bin/op-s6-systemctl` via `nohup` since nothing auto-respawned it). **This should be looked into**: why isn't it under proper s6 supervision, and how was it originally started?
- **`gemma`'s `up` script silently swallows failures**: `/etc/s6/sv/gemma/up` (execline) does `foreground { sh /etc/s6/sv/gemma/shell_up }` then unconditionally `exit 0` — so even though `shell_up` has `set -eu` and would stop correctly on a real failure inside it, s6 never sees that failure; the oneshot always reports success. **Not yet fixed** — needs `foreground` to be replaced with something that propagates the real exit code (e.g. drop the trailing `exit 0` and let the script's own exit code from `shell_up` propagate, or explicit exit-code capture).
- **`xray` was crash-looping** because its config (`/etc/xray/config.json`, a symlink into `/dev/shm/xray-ghostbridge.json` — tmpfs, wiped every reboot) didn't exist post-reboot, since gemma's masked failure meant the regeneration chain (`op-gemma` → `op-identity-shuttle`) never actually completed at boot. **Fixed for this boot** by running both binaries manually as root; `xray` came up clean afterward — but see gemma bug above, this will recur on every reboot until that's fixed.
- **Port 443 conflict**: an Incus proxy device on the `caddy` container (`docker-port-0.0.0.0-443`, set up via `incus compose` importing Netmaker's own docker-compose bundle) was bound to host port 443, competing with `xray`. Per user direction, the `caddy` container was **deleted entirely** (xray already covers reverse-proxy duty; caddy was serving Netmaker's own dashboard/API/broker via SNI routing, now redundant). Confirmed caddy removed cleanly; `xray` restarted via D-Bus and came up stable.

## Current state — IN PROGRESS, left mid-operation

`sudo s6-apply` (the safe, documented, rollback-capable commit+install wrapper at `/usr/local/bin/s6-apply` — read its source, it really does sync→commit→live-install→bootdb-sync atomically with rollback on failure) was run to commit `ollama-srv` (needed for the LLM bring-up; it exists in `/etc/s6/sv/ollama-srv` and shows `active` in the working set, but predates the Jun 20 db currently live, so it's not running) and whatever else has accumulated in `/etc/s6/sv/` since Jun 20.

**It is currently stuck**, confirmed via full process tree (not guessed):
```
s6-apply(20410)
 └ s6-rc-set-install(20423)   [the "s6 live install -b" step]
    └ s6-rc(20424)  -u -- change ovsbr0-static ovsbr0-init opdbus op-web-srv op-projection op-openvswitch-daemon op-dbus-mirror op-dbus op-cognitive-mcp
       └ s6-svlisten(20588)   [waiting for a readiness notification]
          └ s6-ftrigrd(20592) [blocked reading the notification fifo]
```
This is the **exact documented `op-web-srv` wedge** from project memory: `op-web-srv` has `notification-fd=3` but its Rust binary never writes the readiness byte, so `s6-svlisten -U` blocks forever, holding the global s6-rc lock. The Jun 20 fix (removing `notification-fd` from `op-web-srv`/`op-assistant-grpc-srv`) was applied to the *bootdb-pointed-at* db, but this fresh commit compiles from the **current** `/etc/s6/sv/` source tree, which may have regressed/never had that fix applied to the actual source files (only to whatever db existed on Jun 20) — needs verification: check whether `/etc/s6/sv/op-web-srv/notification-fd` currently exists.

**Was about to (not yet done)**: write the readiness byte directly into `op-web-srv`'s open fd 3 (pid 20608, confirmed via `/proc/20608/fd/`) to unstick *this* transition non-destructively (no killing), then separately apply the permanent fix to `/etc/s6/sv/op-web-srv/notification-fd` (and `op-assistant-grpc-srv`) plus the git source at `deploy/s6/op-web-srv/` so future commits don't re-hit this.

**Do NOT kill `s6-apply` or its children carelessly** — per its own design, if it's killed mid-transition rather than allowed to complete or cleanly fail, its rollback logic (which only triggers on a clean non-zero exit, not a hang) won't run, and bootdb could be left pointing at whatever the live system was on before this run (which should still be the safe Jun 20 db at this point, since `s6 set commit` already completed but bootdb hasn't been repointed to the new db yet — so a reboot *right now*, before this resolves, would likely still boot into the Jun 20 db safely, but this hasn't been re-verified since the commit step ran).

## Still open / not yet done

- Fix `gemma`'s `up` script to not swallow failures (see above).
- Permanently fix `op-web-srv`/`op-assistant-grpc-srv` notification-fd in both `/etc/s6/sv/` and `deploy/s6/` git source, then verify a fresh `s6-apply` run doesn't wedge.
- Once the above is resolved: start `ollama-srv` via D-Bus `org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl` `Start`, verify `ollama serve` comes up, verify `gemma4:12b` is reachable and zeroclaw's active provider (`ollama`) works end-to-end.
- `fsck` on `/dev/sda1` (FAT/EFI partition) — dmesg showed "not properly unmounted, some data may be corrupt" from the abrupt reboot during the outage. Not urgent, not yet done.
- Investigate why `op-s6-systemctl`'s process is orphaned/unsupervised rather than a normal s6 longrun — a "why" question, not yet answered.
- PR #15 (`feat/sled-source-port-salt`, security/correctness fixes triaged earlier) was sent to Ultraplan for cloud refinement, approved, and executed remotely as a PR — check GitHub for its actual landing state, not yet re-verified from this session.
- PR #14 (`plugin-capability`) was closed as superseded by #15 — done, no follow-up needed.

## Key files/paths for whoever picks this up

- `/usr/local/bin/s6-apply` — the safe wrapper, read it before running `s6 set commit`/`s6 live install` by hand ever again.
- `/etc/s6/sv/gemma/up` + `shell_up` — the failure-masking bug.
- `/etc/s6/sv/op-web-srv/notification-fd`, `/etc/s6/sv/op-assistant-grpc-srv/notification-fd` — check existence, should not exist.
- `deploy/s6/dbus-session/run` — already correctly edited this session to exec `busd` instead of `dbus-daemon` (busd installed at `/usr/local/bin/busd` v0.5.0) — **this change has never actually gone live yet**; it's sitting in a pending commit that hasn't successfully installed (blocked by all of the above). Once `s6-apply` succeeds cleanly, verify `dbus-session`'s live servicedir actually runs `busd`, not the old `dbus-daemon`.
- Project memory: `project_s6_commit_prune_hazard.md`, `artix-s6-layout.md` — both already updated with prior incidents; this handoff's findings should probably be folded into those after the dust settles.
